record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let P_n and Q_m be homogeneous polynomials of odd degrees n and m with n ≠ m, and consider the planar system ẋ = P_n(x,y), ẏ = Q_m(x,y). Determine whether the maximum possible number of limit cycles of such a system is (n + m)/2.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Is (n +m)/2 the maximum number of limit cycles of ˙x =Pn(x,y ), ˙y =Qm(x,y ) where n̸= m and Pn and Qm are homogeneous polynomials of odd degrees n and m, respectively?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar polynomial differential system
  ẋ = P_n(x, y),   ẏ = Q_m(x, y),
where P_n and Q_m are homogeneous real polynomials in the variables x, y of odd degrees n and m respectively, with n ≠ m. A limit cycle of such a system is an isolated periodic orbit in the phase plane.

Determine whether the maximum possible number of limit cycles that such a system can have is exactly (n + m)/2. Equivalently, prove or disprove that for every choice of odd integers n ≠ m, no such system possesses more than (n + m)/2 limit cycles, and that this bound is attained.
artifact.category_tag: Limit cycles of planar polynomial vector fields
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not reveal any published proof or disproof of the conjectured bound (n+m)/2 for the maximum number of limit cycles of planar systems whose components are homogeneous polynomials of distinct odd degrees. Related research on homogeneous polynomial vector fields (Kukles systems, cyclicity bounds via Lyapunov constants, rigid centers) is active, but no result settling this specific conjecture appears in the search results, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Limit cycles of planar polynomial vector fields - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of known results on limit cycles of planar polynomial vector fields; no general sharp bound for homogeneous-component systems of distinct odd degrees is reported.
status_evidence.claim: No general settled bound is documented for this homogeneous odd-degree configuration.

status_evidence.title: Criteria on the existence of limit cycles in planar polynomial systems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent criteria for existence of limit cycles, but the specific (n+m)/2 conjecture is not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area without a resolution of the conjectured maximum (n+m)/2.
